claim: Higher ad spend is associated with higher return rate
evidence: Pearson r=0.049 p=0.00017 n=6000; lowest ad_spend quartile mean return_rate 0.113 vs mid-high quartiles 0.123 and 0.121; one-way ANOVA across 4 quartiles p=0.00066

claim: More support contacts are associated with lower weekly sales
evidence: Pearson r=-0.031 p=0.016 n=6000; 0-1 contacts mean weekly_sales 161.8 vs >=7 contacts mean 158.2, difference ~3.6, t-test p=0.019 Cohen d=0.097

claim: Weekend ratings are slightly lower than weekday ratings
evidence: Weekday mean 3.742 (n=4280) vs weekend mean 3.688 (n=1720); Welch t p=0.026 Cohen d=0.064; Pearson r=-0.029

claim: Warmer temperature is associated with slightly higher conversion
evidence: Pearson r=0.026 p=0.041 n=6000; coldest quartile converted 28.0% vs warmest quartile 32.2%; binned means rise from 0.275 to 0.314 in warmest bins; chi-square across quartiles p=0.081

claim: Budget segment converts at a higher rate than premium segment
evidence: Budget 30.85% converted (n=2998) vs premium 28.58% (n=3002); chi-square vs converted p=0.058

claim: Faster delivery is associated with slightly higher satisfaction
evidence: Fastest bin <=2.3 days mean satisfaction 79.33 vs slowest >=6.5 days mean 78.34 and 78.30-78.60 in middle bins; Welch t fast vs slow p=0.091 Cohen d=0.086; Pearson r=-0.018

claim: Spend has no meaningful linear predictor among measured variables
evidence: All absolute correlations with spend <0.02, strongest is revenue r=-0.018; binned price vs spend flat 79.4-81.8 across 8 price octiles and discount vs spend flat 79.5-81.5 despite price range 3.6 to 336.3

claim: Loyalty members convert at a slightly higher rate than non-members, the only binary predictor with a significant conversion lift
evidence: conversion 32.4% (loyalty=1, n=1768) vs 29.5% (loyalty=0, n=4232); chi2=4.97, p=0.026

claim: Weekend vs weekday shows no meaningful difference in conversion or repeat purchase
evidence: converted 31.6% weekend vs 29.8% weekday; chi2=1.74, p=0.188; repeat_purchase also ns p=0.308

claim: Ad spend has no linear or binned relationship with weekly sales
evidence: Pearson r=-0.004; binned means across 8 ad_spend quantiles range 156.5-164.5 with no trend (overall mean 159.6, n=6000)

claim: Discount level does not drive conversion or spend
evidence: Pearson r~0.00 with converted and 0.007 with spend; binned conversion flat 0.28-0.32 across 0-30% discount; binned spend flat 80.7-83.0

claim: Price is decoupled from revenue and spend despite wide price range
evidence: Pearson price-revenue r=-0.018, price-spend r=-0.024; binned revenue 35.3-37.8 flat across price octiles; 19 extreme outliers price>200 (max 514.8 vs mean 43.2) without elevated revenue

claim: Satisfaction, rating, support contacts and delivery experience are mutually uncorrelated
evidence: support-satisfaction r=0.015; delivery-rating r=-0.008; rating-satisfaction r=-0.004; binned satisfaction ~77.9-78.9 across support_contacts 0-14, flat

claim: All numeric pairwise correlations are essentially zero; strongest absolute r is only ~0.04
evidence: Full 25x25 matrix max |r|=0.042 (price-noise_num_04); only flagged pair delivery-support r=-0.039 p=0.003 Spearman -0.049 p=0.00015, negligible effect

claim: Region, channel and segment show no meaningful differences in spend, revenue, satisfaction or conversion
evidence: e.g. spend by region East 82.5 North 81.3 South 81.5 West 81.6; by channel app 82.1 store 81.6 web 81.4; ANOVA all p>0.11 except delivery_days segment budget 4.22 vs premium 4.33 F=5.09 p=0.024 and region F=2.82 p=0.038, tiny effects

claim: Conversion rate differs by channel: web converts highest and store lowest
Repeat-purchase rate peaks at exactly 4 support contacts and is lower on either side
evidence: quintile means 39.7% (n=1286), 39.5% (n=1680), 46.7% at 4 contacts (n=687), 38.1% (n=1545), 40.1% (n=802); ANOVA F=3.86 p=0.0039; exact: 4 contacts 46.7% vs 5 contacts 37.2% (n=591) and 6 contacts 37.2% (n=529); full chi-square p=0.045

claim: Price and revenue are both heavily right-skewed but their extremes are independent and uncorrelated
evidence: price skew 2.27 max 359.3 vs p95 95.9 (46 rows >150); revenue skew 2.38 max 332.4 vs p95 83.3 (21 rows >150); only 5 rows have both >100; top-10 price rows have revenues 7-59; top-10 revenue rows have prices 18-59; Pearson r=0.008 p=0.55 n=6000, r=0.013 after excluding price>150

claim: Ad spend has no linear association with weekly sales
evidence: Pearson r=0.008 p=0.52, Spearman r=0.007, n=6000 (SE~0.013, powered to detect |r|>0.04); decile and quintile means flat around 160.7

claim: Discount percentage does not drive conversion or spend
evidence: discount vs converted r=-0.018 p=0.16; decile conversion 28.0-34.8% with no trend; discount vs spend r=-0.025 p=0.057; decile spend means 78.3-82.9 flat, n=6000

claim: Rating is unrelated to satisfaction and support contacts are unrelated to satisfaction
evidence: rating vs satisfaction Pearson r=0.004 p=0.77 Spearman 0.005 n=6000; rating-decile satisfaction means 77.5-79.2 flat; support_contacts vs satisfaction r=-0.012 p=0.37

claim: Loyalty, weekend, region and segment show essentially no differences in spend, revenue or conversion
evidence: spend by loyalty 81.28 vs 81.05; spend by weekend 81.34 vs 80.91; revenue by segment budget 36.45 vs premium 37.04; weekly_sales by region 160.5-160.9; loyalty vs repeat r=0.014 p=0.28; all Pearson |r|<0.03, t-test/chi-square p>0.24 except channel

claim: Spend contains 4 impossible negative values indicating data errors
All designated noise columns behave as pure noise with no signal
evidence: noise_num vs converted |r|<=0.029 and vs spend |r|<=0.022 (n=6000); noise_cat x converted chi-square p=0.391, 0.142, 0.213, 0.837; noise_num means ~0 std ~1.0, noise_cat counts ~1450-1550 per level
